- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.28) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.17) and price is trending down, model may underestimate support; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days if sentiment swings sharply.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.28, -0.22), model tends to lag in recognizing reversal; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
